I keep coming back to this pattern in production; it works with

With Java's Kafka consumer, the code decides exactly when the offset gets committed.
If the consumer rejects the message, the broker will retry it.

I insert the message ID and the business update inside one transaction.

I prefer to reject and let the
retry loop handle it, because a duplicate charge is usually worse than a few minutes of delay.

When the message already has a stored result,
I return it instead of calling the side effect again.
The consumer just sets a fixed value, such as status = shipped.

If you store the result but fail to commit the offset, the

I put both
